questions.question: What distinctive taste is associated with edible acids, such as those found in lemons or vinegar?
What is a base defined as in chemistry?
options: Any substance that reacts with acids to form a salt
A substance that only reacts with water to form an acid
A liquid that turns blue litmus paper red
A metal that produces hydrogen gas when heated

questions.question: What is an alkali?
options: An insoluble base that cannot dissolve in water
A soluble base that forms an alkaline solution
A type of acid that turns litmus paper red
A gas produced when metals react with water

questions.question: Why do some concentrated acids and alkalis carry a warning symbol showing a hand being damaged?
options: They are flammable and catch fire easily
They are corrosive and can cause chemical burns
They are highly toxic if breathed in
They can easily dissolve glass containers

questions.question: How does litmus paper behave in the presence of acids and alkalis?
options: Acid turns red litmus blue; alkali turns blue litmus red
Acid turns blue litmus red; alkali turns red litmus blue
Acid turns blue litmus green; alkali turns red litmus yellow
Acid has no effect on litmus; alkali turns both types red

questions.question: What are the two products formed when a metal reacts with an acid?
options: A metal salt and oxygen gas
A metal oxide and carbon dioxide gas
A metal salt and hydrogen gas

questions.question: What is the standard chemical test for hydrogen gas?
options: It turns damp blue litmus paper red
It makes a squeaky pop sound when tested with a lit splint

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct word equation for the reaction of a metal carbonate with an acid?
options: metal carbonate + acid → metal salt + hydrogen
metal carbonate + acid → metal salt + water + carbon dioxide
metal carbonate + acid → metal oxide + water
metal carbonate + acid → metal salt + oxygen + carbon dioxide

questions.question: How can you test a gas to show that it is carbon dioxide?
options: Bubble the gas through limewater and watch it turn cloudy
Hold a lit splint near the gas and listen for a squeaky pop
Hold a glowing splint near the gas and see if it relights
Pass the gas over blue litmus paper and watch it turn blue

questions.question: What do we call rain water when it becomes significantly more acidic than normal?
What happens when acid rain reacts with a building made of marble?
options: It forms a metal oxide and protects the marble from further damage
It reacts to produce a salt, water, and carbon dioxide, using up some of the marble
It turns the marble into pure hydrogen gas which escapes
It has no chemical reaction because marble is completely insoluble

questions.question: What is the general word equation for a neutralisation reaction between a base and an acid?
What are the correct chemical formulas for sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid respectively?
Which of the following groups of substances are common bases?
What does the state symbol (aq) represent in a chemical equation?
options: A substance dissolved in water (aqueous solution)

questions.question: What are the products when a metal oxide reacts with an acid?
What type of solution is formed when a non-metal oxide dissolves in water?
options: A salt solution with no pH change

questions.question: How is the concentration of hydrogen ions related to the pH of an acid?
options: The higher the concentration of hydrogen, the higher the pH
The higher the concentration of hydrogen, the lower the pH
The concentration of hydrogen does not affect the pH
Low concentrations of hydrogen always result in a pH of 14

questions.question: Since the pH scale goes up and down in factors of ten, how much more acidic is an acid of pH 2 compared to an acid of pH 3?
What color does red cabbage indicator turn when added to a neutral solution?
